hook.title: One engine, different dashboards
hook.text: A GNN is an engine that turns a graph into a table of node embeddings. What you read off the engine depends on the **dashboard** you bolt on. Want a verdict per **node**? Add a small readout on each row. A verdict per **pair** (edge)? Read two rows together: concatenate them or take a dot product. A verdict for the **whole graph**? Pool all rows into one summary (mean, max or sum). Same engine; different instruments.
hook.recall: Remember the dashboards: node head = readout per row; edge head = combine two rows (concat+linear or dot product); graph head = pool every row (mean/max/sum).

explore.intro: Embeddings of four nodes (d = 3). Switch heads and pooling.
tasks: Graph tab: add identical nodes. Which pooling changes? Which doesn’t?
Edge tab: compute the dot product by hand and check it.
explore.takeaway: $\hat y_v=W_{head}h_v^{(L)}$ (node), $\hat y_{vu}=\text{Linear}(\text{Concat}(h_v,h_u))$ or $h_v^\top h_u$ (edge), $\hat y_G=\text{Mean/Max/Sum}(\{h_v\})$ (graph). Losses: cross-entropy (classification), MSE (regression).

items: Predictions compared with labels → loss function (and evaluation metrics)
build.explanation: Input graph → GNN → node embeddings → prediction head → predictions; with labels they feed the loss function and evaluation metrics.

options: $\hat y_v=W_{head}h_v^{(L)}$ with $W_{head}\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}$, then softmax
A dot product with a random vector

questions.prompt: Edge-level head “concatenation + linear” with $d=64$-dimensional node embeddings. What is the input dimension of the Linear layer?
questions.explanation: Concat of two $d$-dim vectors is $2d=128$ (slide: Linear maps $2d$-dim to $k$-dim).

options: A dot-product edge head applies directly to 1-way prediction (e.g. link prediction)
For $k$-way edge prediction you can use $k$ trainable matrices $W^{(1..k)}$
Graph-level heads can use global mean, max or sum pooling
Global sum pooling is unaffected by the number of nodes in the graph
questions.explanation: Sum grows with the number of nodes; mean normalises (try it in the explorer).

options: Cross-entropy for classification; MSE (L2 loss) for regression

questions.prompt: *“I can use a node-level head to classify whole graphs by just reading the first node.”* What is the issue?
options: A graph-level task needs a graph-level head that combines *all* node embeddings (e.g. global mean/max/sum pooling)
